P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No surrender rule, but the banking system is impaired. Since 2019, banks have imposed informal capital controls through Central Bank circulars, with no formal capital-controls law, and pre-October 2019 dollar deposits remain largely frozen (about USD 93bn per July 2026 reports). Newly transferred 'fresh dollar' accounts and cards function. Keep foreign income in fresh-dollar accounts or regulated channels.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Lebanon applies territoriality. Salaries are taxable if the beneficiary is resident in Lebanon, or if the services are performed on Lebanese territory even when paid from abroad. Profits of individuals (business and professional income) are taxed at progressive rates of 4% to 25%; payroll tax brackets run from 2% to 25% (2022 Budget Law). Deloitte 2026 confirms business-income rates from 4% (up to LBP 540 million) to 25% (over LBP 13.5 billion).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 11%. Exports of goods and services and export-related services are zero-rated, and banking, financial and insurance services are exempt. The registration threshold was not captured. Kintsugi (2026): registration is mandatory once taxable turnover exceeds LBP 5 billion (2024 Budget Law), measured over one to four consecutive quarters; importers and exporters register regardless of turnover.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed). The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
